diff_ref: git diff 9997c32d..HEAD -- scripts/checklist_engine.py tests/test_checklist_engine.py docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md (branch epic-418/a2-467-trip-semantics, head 70e2d779; engine delta +109 lines: _append_trip_entry, begin_over_line_records, _trip_hard_gate, _trip_advisory HARD branch, dispatch)

smells.finding: The two new functions are 12 and 20 lines of body. _trip_hard_gate grows by 8 lines and stays a single linear guard with one branch. _trip_advisory's HARD branch gains one computation and two '+ ledger_note' suffixes; no new nesting level.
scripts/checklist_engine.py is a ~3200-line single module and this change adds two more module-level functions to it.

override.repo_standard: docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md and the engine's own structure: the checklist engine is deliberately ONE self-contained script so an installed skill bundle can vendor a single file, and the reviewer/implementer/workbench skills each ship a copy of it. references/checklist-engine.md documents that vendoring.
override.reason: Splitting the engine into modules would break the single-file vendoring the whole skill-distribution model rests on. The Trip section is also already a coherent named region within the file, and this change stays inside it rather than scattering.

smells.finding: Actively avoided, and this is the change's central design property. The compliance fact is computed exactly once (ledger_note, above both HARD sub-branch returns) and rendered at exactly one site -- I verified with grep (1 'TRIP LEDGER' occurrence in scripts/) and an ast scan (callers_of(begin_over_line_records) == ['_trip_advisory']). The 'hard' value written into the entry is resolved from the same _gauge_reader.thresholds_for call shape used a line above, deliberately so the two cannot disagree.

begin_over_line_records reads only cl['trip_ledger'] and _latest_why_record(cl) -- both checklist-state concerns, in the module that owns checklist state. _append_trip_entry touches only the ledger it owns. Neither reaches into another object's internals.

(reading, hard) travel together as a pair through _trip_hard_gate into _append_trip_entry, and the same pair is re-resolved by _trip_advisory for its own render. The engine already has the makings of a 'band judgment' value (fill + hard + model + gate) and this change makes the third site that assembles it by hand. Non-blocking and NOT worth changing inside this diff -- introducing a value object here would touch the Trip section g2 and g3 just shipped, which the handoff excludes. Recorded as an observation for a later Trip-section consolidation.

'outcome' is a bare string with exactly two legal values, and the legal set is written out as a tuple literal in the selector while the writer passes the strings at its two call sites -- three places that must agree by convention. A module-level constant (or the two strings named once) would make N10's defect shape structurally impossible rather than test-caught. Non-blocking: the schema doc pins both values, mutation N10 kills the filter, and the whole surface is 4 lines.

_append_trip_entry(cl, gate, verb, outcome, reading, hard, why_ref) takes 7 parameters, five of which are the entry's own fields. This is the same observation as the data-clumps one from the other side: the natural refactor is to pass the band judgment as one value. Non-blocking -- it is a private helper with a single caller, so the argument order cannot drift across call sites, and both call sites are three lines apart.

The opposite: adding this capability required edits in one region of one file (plus a signature and one call at the dispatch chokepoint). Nothing outside scripts/checklist_engine.py had to change for the mechanism to work.

_trip_hard_gate now does two things (judge, and record the judgment), but they are one concern -- the record IS the judgment -- and the alternative (a second evaluation site) is the duplication the handoff explicitly forbids.
No chain longer than one hop. reading.fill_fraction / reading.model are single attribute reads; the ledger is reached by cl.get('trip_ledger') and nothing navigates through it.

Nothing is built for a future caller. No new verb, no new flag, no --json surface, no configuration hook. The 'outcome' vocabulary is closed at two values and the selector rejects anything else rather than accommodating it. The one field added beyond the plan (why_ref) is load-bearing for the shipped predicate, not a hook -- see check a1-whyref.

The comment-to-code ratio in the new engine code is unusually high: _append_trip_entry is 12 lines of body under 14 lines of docstring, begin_over_line_records is 20 under 21, and there are inline block comments at both write sites and at the fail-safe return.

override.repo_standard: The repo's shipped house style for scripts/checklist_engine.py, visible throughout the pre-existing file (e.g. _latest_why_record, has_pending_refresh_request, main()'s refusals block) and reinforced by references/global-crew.md's requirement that a decision be traceable to its issue: comments here carry the ISSUE NUMBER and the reason a branch exists, not a restatement of the code.
override.reason: These comments are not covering for unclear code -- the code they sit on is short and plain. They record WHY (which #-issue forced the branch, why the fail-safe returns before writing, why advance is deliberately not a write site). That is the durable-context requirement the repo imposes on this file, and it subordinates the smell. The one place I would push back is stylistic, not structural, so it is not raised as a finding.
